newsitem.title: USA: Mass killer Manson found guilty in prison drug case.
newsitem.headline: Mass killer Manson found guilty in prison drug case.

text.p: Mass murderer Charles Manson was in solitary confinement on Tuesday after being found guilty of drug-trafficking inside the California prison where he is jailed for masterminding a bloody 1969 rampage, officials said.

In addition to the punishment by a prison panel, a formal investigation of the drug offences at Corcoran State Prison, about 150 miles (240 km) north of Los Angeles, was under way, spokeswoman Sylvia Gonzalez said.
After the prison completes its investigation, Manson could face trial in prison on other drug charges, she said.

Manson, one of the world's most notorious criminals, was originally sentenced to die in the gas chamber for masterminding the 1969 killings of actress Sharon Tate -- the pregnant wife of film director Roman Polanski -- and six other people.

The head of the so-called "Manson family" was convicted of ordering his followers to carry out the murders during a two-day rampage in the Los Angeles area. Manson hoped the slayings would ignite a race war.

His sentence, and those of other Death Row inmates, was later reduced to life in prison when the state Supreme Court declared the death penalty unconstitutional. California later restored capital punishment.
In March Manson was denied parole for the ninth time.
Prison officials said on Tuesday they could not provide details about Manson's alleged drug offences until the investigation was completed.

Gonzalez said Manson was removed from the general prison population and placed in confinement, commonly referred to by inmates as the "hole." He will remain in confinement throughout the investigation, she said.
"He's going to be going through a due process investigation," she said. "We don't know how long it will take."
